dubai.weather_note: November to March is temperate. Avoid June to September when heat is severe.
dubai.perfect_if: You want polished five-star ease, tax-free shopping and a beach-and-brunch rhythm three hours from home.
dubai.skip_if: You are drawn to old-world texture, deep history or quiet, unmanicured places.
dubai.teaser: A city built for arrival, where the service rarely misses a beat.

singapore-city.weather_note: Warm and humid year-round with brief showers. Slightly drier February to April.
singapore-city.perfect_if: You want a spotless, effortless city that families and first-timers navigate without friction.
singapore-city.skip_if: You are looking for wilderness, spontaneity or a bargain.
singapore-city.teaser: Order and abundance in equal measure, delivered without fuss.

kuala-lumpur.weather_note: Tropical throughout with afternoon rain. May to July and December to February are the steadier windows.
kuala-lumpur.perfect_if: You want a warm, value-rich Asian city with easy food and no visa to arrange.
kuala-lumpur.skip_if: You want a marquee destination or refined, understated luxury.
kuala-lumpur.teaser: A generous, unhurried city that asks little and gives plenty.

siem-reap.weather_note: November to February is dry and comfortable. Avoid the March-May heat and summer monsoon.
siem-reap.perfect_if: You want Angkor at dawn and a handful of genuinely fine hotels in a quiet, low-key town.
siem-reap.skip_if: You need a beach, nightlife or a busy itinerary beyond the temples.
siem-reap.teaser: A single, unforgettable ruin, and the stillness that surrounds it.

seoul.weather_note: Spring blossom and autumn colour are the peaks. Skip the humid July-August and the deep winter cold.
seoul.perfect_if: You want a fast, modern city with deep tradition, remarkable food and immaculate safety.
seoul.skip_if: You want beaches, warmth or a relaxed, slow pace.
seoul.teaser: Ancient palaces and a restless present, side by side.

galle.weather_note: The south coast is at its best December to March. Avoid the May-September monsoon.
galle.perfect_if: You want a Dutch-fort town, boutique villas and a slow coast an hour's flight away.
galle.skip_if: You want big resorts, nightlife or a packed sightseeing agenda.
galle.teaser: A walled town by the sea, kept at the pace of the tide.

london.weather_note: Late spring and early autumn are the kindest. Expect grey and rain the rest of the year.
london.perfect_if: You want theatre, tailoring, museums and the finest Indian food outside India.
london.skip_if: You are on a tight budget or want reliable sunshine.
london.teaser: The city that rewards those who already know their way around it.

milan.weather_note: Spring and early autumn are ideal. August empties out and much closes; winter is foggy.
milan.perfect_if: You want fashion, design and aperitivo, and Lake Como an hour up the road.
milan.skip_if: You want ruins and postcard Italy over style and shopping.
milan.teaser: Italy's most quietly confident city, dressed for the occasion.

barcelona.weather_note: Late spring and September balance warmth with lighter crowds. July-August is hot and packed.
barcelona.perfect_if: You want Gaudi, a beach in the city and long, late Mediterranean dinners.
barcelona.skip_if: You dislike crowds and are wary of pickpockets in busy quarters.
barcelona.teaser: A seaside city with an architect's imagination and no early nights.

santorini.weather_note: May-June and September are warm and calmer. July-August is crowded; winter is shut.
santorini.perfect_if: You want the caldera view, a cave suite and a honeymoon that photographs itself.
santorini.skip_if: You want variety, nightlife or space away from other couples in peak season.
santorini.teaser: White walls above a drowned volcano, made for two.

zermatt.weather_note: January-March for skiing, July-August for hiking under the Matterhorn. Shoulder months are quiet.
zermatt.perfect_if: You want a car-free Alpine village with the Matterhorn at your window and grand-hotel comfort.
zermatt.skip_if: You want warmth, a beach or a low bill.
zermatt.teaser: One mountain, always in view, and a village that lives around it.

prague.weather_note: Late spring and early autumn are mild and clear. December brings Christmas markets; winter is cold.
prague.perfect_if: You want a walkable old city of spires, castles and easy charm.
prague.skip_if: You need a beach, big luxury names or warm weather.
prague.teaser: A hundred spires and a river, largely spared by time.

budapest.weather_note: Spring and early autumn are the most pleasant. Winter is cold; midsummer can be hot.
budapest.perfect_if: You want grand riverside architecture, thermal baths and honest value.
budapest.skip_if: You want marquee luxury, a coastline or guaranteed sun.
budapest.teaser: A capital of thermal water and faded grandeur on the Danube.

cape-town.weather_note: November to March is the warm, dry summer. Avoid the wet, windy winter of June-August.
cape-town.perfect_if: You want a mountain-meets-ocean city, world-class wine and safari within reach.
cape-town.skip_if: You want to wander freely at night without watching your surroundings.
cape-town.teaser: A city under a flat-topped mountain, with the wine country at its back.

san-francisco.weather_note: September-October is the warmest and clearest. Summer is famously foggy and cool.
san-francisco.perfect_if: You want the bay, the bridge and Napa wine country an hour north.
san-francisco.skip_if: You are unprepared for the visa wait, or want warmth and a low bill.
san-francisco.teaser: Fog, hills and the wine country just beyond them.

mexico-city.weather_note: The dry season, November to April, is best. Skip the June-September afternoon rains.
mexico-city.perfect_if: You are a serious food and culture traveller who holds a US visa and wants the real thing.
mexico-city.skip_if: You want an easy, short-haul trip or you are nervous about a big city.
mexico-city.teaser: A vast, art-heavy capital where the food alone justifies the journey. A valid US visa waives the visa requirement.

cusco.weather_note: The dry season, May to September, is best for Machu Picchu. Avoid the January-March rains.
cusco.perfect_if: You want Machu Picchu and the Sacred Valley, and you already hold a US or Schengen visa.
cusco.skip_if: You have limited time, altitude concerns or want a low-effort holiday.
cusco.teaser: The Inca heartland, reached by long haul and a train through the mountains. Visa-free for holders of a US, UK, Schengen, Canada or Australia visa.

delhi.weather_note: October-November and February-March are pleasant. Avoid the May-June heat and January smog.
delhi.perfect_if: You want Mughal monuments, layered history and the gateway to the Golden Triangle.
delhi.skip_if: You want calm, clean air or a beach.
delhi.teaser: Seven cities stacked on one, and the door to the north.

udaipur.weather_note: October to February is cool and lake-full. Avoid the searing April-June summer.
udaipur.perfect_if: You want lake palaces and India's most romantic hotels without leaving the country.
udaipur.skip_if: You want a beach, nightlife or cool mountain air.
udaipur.teaser: Palaces set on water, and the country's finest hotels among them.

varanasi.weather_note: October to March is cool and clear for the ghats. Avoid the summer heat and monsoon floods.
varanasi.perfect_if: You want the Ganges at dawn and one of the oldest living cities on earth.
varanasi.skip_if: You are unsettled by crowds, intensity or open displays of ritual and death.
varanasi.teaser: The river, the fire and the dawn, as they have been for millennia.

alleppey.weather_note: November to March is dry and green. Avoid the June-September monsoon, though some seek it for Ayurveda.
alleppey.perfect_if: You want a private houseboat on the backwaters and unhurried Kerala calm.
alleppey.skip_if: You want sightseeing, nightlife or a fast-moving itinerary.
alleppey.teaser: A slow drift through the backwaters, with the day set by the water.

hyderabad.weather_note: October to February is the pleasant window. Avoid the hot April-June stretch.
hyderabad.perfect_if: You want Nizami grandeur, the biryani of record and a landmark palace hotel.
hyderabad.skip_if: You want a beach, hills or a marquee holiday destination.
hyderabad.teaser: A city of pearls and biryani, still keeping its old courtly manners.

abu-dhabi.weather_note: Best from November to March; the summer months are severe with heat well into the forties.
abu-dhabi.perfect_if: You want the polish of the Gulf with more calm and culture than its neighbour, and the Louvre on your doorstep.
abu-dhabi.skip_if: You want nightlife and buzz; this is the quieter, more considered emirate.
abu-dhabi.teaser: The Gulf at a lower volume, where grand ambitions are kept behind a composed front.

doha.weather_note: November to March is the window; summer is intensely hot and best avoided.
doha.perfect_if: You want a compact, refined Gulf stay built around world-class museums and a short, easy flight.
doha.skip_if: You want a week of variety; Doha rewards a focused few days more than a long stay.
doha.teaser: A small capital with serious taste, its treasures gathered close to the water.

muscat.weather_note: October to March is mild and pleasant; from May to September the heat is intense.
muscat.perfect_if: You want Arabia with its dignity intact - forts, wadis and empty coast rather than glass towers.
muscat.skip_if: You want nightlife, big shopping and constant motion; Oman is deliberately gentle.
muscat.teaser: Old Arabia, kept low and honest, where the mountains meet a quiet sea.

amman-petra.weather_note: Spring and autumn are ideal; summer is hot in the desert and winter can be cold in Amman.
amman-petra.perfect_if: You want Petra, Wadi Rum and the Dead Sea threaded into one unhurried, deeply historic journey.
amman-petra.skip_if: You want beaches, shopping or a resort week; this is a trip for the curious traveller.
amman-petra.teaser: A rose-red city and a red desert, held quietly at the crossroads of the ancient world.

bangkok.weather_note: November to February is cooler and dry; avoid the hot April and the wet months from June to October.
bangkok.perfect_if: You want a great-value luxury city break - fine hotels, brilliant food and easy visa-free entry.
bangkok.skip_if: You want quiet and calm; Bangkok is loud, dense and always in motion.
bangkok.teaser: A city of river light and long dinners, generous to anyone who arrives hungry.

phuket.weather_note: November to March is dry and calm; May to October brings monsoon rain and rough seas.
phuket.perfect_if: You want a beach week with world-class resorts, island-hopping and quiet coves within reach.
phuket.skip_if: You want an untouched, undiscovered shore; Phuket's coast is developed and busy in parts.
phuket.teaser: The Andaman at its most indulgent, with the quiet bays kept for those who ask.

krabi.weather_note: November to March is the dry season; the monsoon from May to October brings heavy rain.
krabi.perfect_if: You want limestone cliffs, calm water and a slower, more scenic side of the Thai coast.
krabi.skip_if: You want nightlife and a busy scene; Krabi is quieter and more about the landscape.
krabi.teaser: Where the karst towers rise straight from the sea, and the days keep their own slow time.

bali.weather_note: April to October is dry and best; the wet season from November to March brings heavy afternoon rain.
bali.perfect_if: You want cliff-edge villas, ricefield calm and a honeymoon that balances beach with real culture.
bali.skip_if: You want a short, easy hop; the flight is long and the south can be crowded.
bali.teaser: An island that still keeps its rituals, offered up between the rice and the sea.

langkawi.weather_note: December to March is driest and calmest; the wetter months run from July to October.
langkawi.perfect_if: You want a quiet duty-free island of rainforest and empty beach, paired with a city stop.
langkawi.skip_if: You want lively nightlife or a wide choice of dining; Langkawi is calm and low-key.
langkawi.teaser: A rainforest island edged in sand, where the loudest sound is often the sea.

hanoi.weather_note: Autumn and spring are mild and clear; summer is hot and wet, winter grey and damp.
hanoi.perfect_if: You want old-quarter atmosphere, brilliant street food and Halong Bay a short drive away.
hanoi.skip_if: You want beaches and resorts; Hanoi is a city of culture, not a place to lie still.
hanoi.teaser: A city of narrow lanes and slow coffee, with the bay held quietly to the east.

ho-chi-minh-city.weather_note: December to March is dry and best; the wet season from May to October brings daily downpours.
ho-chi-minh-city.perfect_if: You want energy, history and superb food, with the Mekong Delta within easy reach.
ho-chi-minh-city.skip_if: You want calm and space; the city is fast, dense and relentless in its traffic.
ho-chi-minh-city.teaser: A city that runs on its own current, fast and warm and unmistakably alive.

hoi-an.weather_note: February to May is dry and pleasant; the wettest months and flood risk come between October and December.
hoi-an.perfect_if: You want a lantern-lit old town, a nearby beach and tailoring and food that stay with you.
hoi-an.skip_if: You want a city buzz or nightlife; Hoi An is romantic, gentle and slow by nature.
hoi-an.teaser: A riverside town lit by lanterns, where an older Vietnam has been quietly kept.

new-york.weather_note: Late spring and early autumn are kindest; skip the humid deep summer and the January freeze.
new-york.perfect_if: You want the full weight of a great world city — galleries, tables, theatre, and shopping in a single week.
new-york.skip_if: You are after quiet, nature, or a slow pace; this city never fully exhales.
new-york.teaser: The one city that rewards ambition — arrive with a list and let it out-pace you.

dubrovnik.weather_note: Come in late spring or September for warm seas without the July crowds and cruise-ship crush.
dubrovnik.perfect_if: You want a walled old town, Adriatic swims, and boat days combined into one unhurried week.
dubrovnik.skip_if: You need direct flights, plentiful Indian food, or a lively city that runs late.
dubrovnik.teaser: A stone city on the Adriatic, best taken slowly and just off the peak.

reykjavik.weather_note: June to August for the midnight sun and open roads; September to March for the northern lights and hard weather.
reykjavik.perfect_if: You want raw landscape — glaciers, geysers, and hot springs — used as a base for the Ring Road.
reykjavik.skip_if: You want warmth, beaches, or Indian food on tap; this is cold, costly, and elemental.
reykjavik.teaser: A small northern capital that exists mostly to send you out into the landscape.

auckland.weather_note: Go Feb-Mar or Nov-Dec for warm, settled days; skip the wet, cool Jun-Aug winter.
auckland.perfect_if: You want a gentle, green gateway to New Zealand with harbour sailing, island vineyards and easy day-trips.
auckland.skip_if: You are chasing the dramatic alpine scenery and adrenaline that live on the South Island, not the North.
auckland.teaser: A harbour city where the vineyards begin a short ferry ride from your table.

cairo.weather_note: Go in the cooler months (Oct-Mar); avoid the fierce Jun-Aug desert heat.
cairo.perfect_if: You want the Pyramids, the new Grand Egyptian Museum and a Nile-led week of deep history.
cairo.skip_if: You need calm, orderly streets or a pure relaxation trip; Cairo is dense and chaotic.
cairo.teaser: The Pyramids on one horizon, a restless river city on the other, and five thousand years in between.

shanghai.weather_note: Spring and October are mild and clear; skip the humid July-August heat and the damp winter chill.
shanghai.perfect_if: You want a fast, cosmopolitan city break with world-class dining, skyline views and serious shopping.
shanghai.skip_if: You want nature, quiet or an unfiltered, budget-first experience.
shanghai.teaser: The Bund at dusk, and a city that never stops rewriting its own skyline.

toronto.weather_note: Late spring and autumn are the sweet spot; winters are severely cold and mid-summer can be humid.
toronto.perfect_if: You want a diverse, easy North American city with excellent Indian food and Niagara within reach.
toronto.skip_if: You want a short-haul trip or a compact, walk-everywhere destination.
toronto.teaser: A city of every cuisine on earth, with the Falls an hour down the road.

vancouver.weather_note: June to September is dry and glorious; the rest of the year is famously grey and wet.
vancouver.perfect_if: You want mountains, ocean and forest at the edge of a relaxed city, with Whistler close by.
vancouver.skip_if: You want guaranteed sun outside summer or a fast, urban-only break.
vancouver.teaser: Ocean on one side, mountains on the other, and Whistler two hours north.

tokyo.weather_note: Cherry blossom late March-April and crisp autumn colour in Oct-Nov are finest; avoid the humid, wet rainy season of June and the heavy heat of August.
tokyo.perfect_if: You want a precise, endlessly layered city where three-Michelin dining, quiet temples and next-day fashion sit within a single afternoon.
tokyo.skip_if: You are after a slow beach reset or want a single unhurried base rather than a dense, fast-moving metropolis.
tokyo.teaser: A city that rewards the curious traveller, where the finest sushi counter and a silent shrine share the same street.

kyoto.weather_note: Come for cherry blossom (late Mar-early Apr) or autumn colour (Nov); avoid the hot, humid rains of Jun-Aug.
kyoto.perfect_if: You want temples, tea houses and ryokan quiet, and you value ritual and restraint over spectacle.
kyoto.skip_if: You need beaches, nightlife, or reliable Indian food, or you are travelling with restless young children.
kyoto.teaser: Old Japan kept whole: raked gardens, wooden lanes, and a kaiseki dinner served like a private ceremony.

hong-kong.weather_note: October to December is dry and comfortable; skip the humid, typhoon-prone June-to-September window.
hong-kong.perfect_if: You want a fast, polished city of harbour views, Michelin dining and serious shopping within a five-hour flight.
hong-kong.skip_if: You are after quiet nature, beaches or a slow, unhurried pace.
hong-kong.teaser: A vertical city where the harbour, the markets and the tasting menus all run late into the night.

taipei.weather_note: Come in spring or autumn for mild, dry days; avoid the humid heat and typhoons of June to September.
taipei.perfect_if: You want a warm, effortless Asian city where night markets, hot-spring retreats and mountain trails sit half an hour apart.
taipei.skip_if: You are chasing beaches, big-brand luxury nightlife or a grand-monument bucket list.
taipei.teaser: A city that rewards the curious: mountain temples by morning, a hot-spring soak by dusk, and a night market that never quite ends.

colombo.weather_note: December to March is dry and clear on the west coast; avoid the May-September southwest monsoon.
colombo.perfect_if: You want a short, low-effort island break with colonial-era streets, sea air and unhurried days a couple of hours from home.
colombo.skip_if: You are chasing dramatic landscapes or a marquee destination — Colombo is a gateway city, not the headline.
colombo.teaser: A harbour capital of tea-house mornings and Indian Ocean evenings, an hour or two from the runway.

geneva.weather_note: May–September for the lake and Alps; skip cold, grey Nov–Feb unless pairing with ski.
geneva.perfect_if: You want a calm, polished lakeside base for watches, wellness and easy Alpine day-trips.
geneva.skip_if: You want buzz, nightlife or a bargain; Geneva is quiet and expensive.
geneva.teaser: A composed lakeside city where the mountains, the watchmakers and the water all keep good time.

kathmandu.weather_note: Come October-November or March-April for clear skies and mountain views; avoid the June-September monsoon and the January cold snap.
kathmandu.perfect_if: You want ancient temple squares, Himalayan air and a gateway to the mountains without a long-haul flight or any visa paperwork.
kathmandu.skip_if: You are after beaches, polished resorts or a seamless big-city experience; Kathmandu is dusty, chaotic and low on luxury infrastructure.
kathmandu.teaser: Living temple cities in a valley beneath the Himalaya, a short flight and no visa away.

paris.weather_note: Late spring and early autumn are kindest; skip August heat and closures, and grey wet January.
paris.perfect_if: You want grand museums, three-star tables and quiet luxury within walking distance of each other.
paris.skip_if: You are chasing beaches, wilderness or an unhurried resort week doing nothing.
paris.teaser: The city that set the standard for how a week away should feel.

porto.weather_note: Late spring and early autumn are warm and dry; winters are wet, summers busy.
porto.perfect_if: You love port cellars, riverside tiles and unhurried food-and-wine days.
porto.skip_if: You want beaches, big-ticket sights or a fast-moving metropolis.
porto.teaser: Port lodges, azulejo facades and the Douro sliding past your table.

lake-como.weather_note: Come late spring or September for warm light on the water; avoid humid, crowded high August.
lake-como.perfect_if: You want a slow, romantic lakeside week of villas, boats and long lunches.
lake-como.skip_if: You want nightlife, big-city energy or a beach holiday.
lake-como.teaser: A quiet water between the mountains, where the days are measured in boat rides and long lunches.

male-maldives.weather_note: Dry season November to April is the window; avoid the June-September monsoon and its rough seas.
male-maldives.perfect_if: You want an overwater villa, a private house reef and nothing on the agenda but each other.
male-maldives.skip_if: You need a city, a night scene or things to do beyond the resort's shoreline.
male-maldives.teaser: One island, one villa, one horizon that belongs to you for the week.

zurich.weather_note: June to September for lakes and alpine trails; December to February for the ski months.
zurich.perfect_if: You want a lakeside base, effortless trains and the Alps an hour away.
zurich.skip_if: You are watching the budget or want warmth and a beach.
zurich.teaser: A quiet, exacting city where the mountains are only a train away.

amsterdam.weather_note: April to June for long light and the tulips; September is calm and mild. Avoid the grey, wet, dark stretch from November to February.
amsterdam.perfect_if: You want a walkable, cultured European city of canals and world-class museums taken at an unhurried pace.
amsterdam.skip_if: You are chasing sun, beaches, or dramatic landscape; Amsterdam is a compact, urban, weather-dependent city.
amsterdam.teaser: A city of canals and quiet mastery, best read slowly, one bridge at a time.

rome.weather_note: Spring and early autumn are ideal; avoid the hot, crowded July-August and the grey damp of deep winter.
rome.perfect_if: You want to walk through three thousand years of art, ruins and living street life, then eat exceptionally well every night.
rome.skip_if: You are chasing beaches, wilderness or a quiet resort escape with no crowds.
rome.teaser: The city where antiquity, faith and appetite share the same cobblestones.

venice.weather_note: Spring and early autumn are finest; skip July-August heat and crowds, and November-December acqua alta flooding.
venice.perfect_if: You want to drift through canals and Renaissance galleries with nowhere urgent to be, ideally two people and a quiet palazzo.
venice.skip_if: You need beaches, nightlife, or children with energy to burn — the crowds and prices will wear you down.
venice.teaser: A city that keeps its own time, where every turn ends at water.

florence.weather_note: Spring and early autumn are gentlest; skip July and August, when the city turns hot, humid and crowded.
florence.perfect_if: You want to live inside the Renaissance for a few days, with long lunches, quiet churches and world-class galleries.
florence.skip_if: You are after beaches, nightlife or nature; Florence is a walkable art city, not a resort.
florence.teaser: The Renaissance kept a city, and it still receives guests one unhurried morning at a time.

amalfi-coast.weather_note: May-June and September-October are warm and calm; avoid July-August crowds and heat, and November-March when many hotels close.
amalfi-coast.perfect_if: You want long lunches over the sea, a boat to Capri, and cliffside towns with nowhere to rush to.
amalfi-coast.skip_if: You want big-resort beaches, nightlife, or an easy step-free trip — the coast is all stairs and switchbacks.
amalfi-coast.teaser: Lemon terraces, a wooden boat waiting, and afternoons that answer to no clock.

madrid.weather_note: Spring and early autumn are ideal; skip July-August when the city empties and bakes in heat.
madrid.perfect_if: You want a European capital with world-class art, late dinners and a warm, unhurried pace of living.
madrid.skip_if: You are after beaches, dramatic landscapes or a quiet retreat away from a busy city.
madrid.teaser: The Prado before lunch, and dinner that begins when other cities are asleep.

lima.weather_note: Come December to April for clear skies and warmth; avoid May to October, when the coastal garua fog greys the city.
lima.perfect_if: You came to Peru for the food and want a few nights in the world's finest kitchens before Machu Picchu.
lima.skip_if: You want a beach or a self-contained resort week; Lima is a working coastal capital, not a place to unwind for seven days.
lima.teaser: The Pacific on one side, a dozen of the world's best tables on the other, and the gateway to the Andes at your back.

lisbon.weather_note: Spring and early autumn are the sweet spot; skip July-August crowds and heat, and the wet grey of December-February.
lisbon.perfect_if: You want an unhurried European capital of tiled facades, river light and long lunches, paired easily with Porto and the Douro.
lisbon.skip_if: You need beaches, nightlife-first energy or a single marquee sight to build a trip around.
lisbon.teaser: A capital that rewards those who slow down: hillside light, river air, and dinners that run late without meaning to.

athens.weather_note: Come in spring or early autumn. Skip July-August, when the city empties and the heat turns oppressive.
athens.perfect_if: You want to walk through the birthplace of Western civilisation, then eat and drink well in a city that has quietly become one of Europe's most exciting.
athens.skip_if: You are chasing beaches or resort calm — Athens is a dense, layered city, best paired with the islands for that.
athens.teaser: The Acropolis at dusk, a rooftop table beneath it, and a city that wears three thousand years lightly.

mykonos.weather_note: Late May to June and September are warm and clear; avoid July-August crowds and the strong meltemi wind, and the November-March low season when the island shuts down.
mykonos.perfect_if: You want polished Cycladic glamour, beach clubs and a yacht day, with dinners that run late.
mykonos.skip_if: You are travelling with young children or want quiet, unspoilt island life away from the scene.
mykonos.teaser: White-on-blue by day, and a long, unhurried table by night.

munich.weather_note: Late spring through early autumn is easy and green; late September for Oktoberfest, December for the Christmas markets.
munich.perfect_if: You want an orderly, handsome city as a base for the Alps, the beer halls, and the castles beyond.
munich.skip_if: You want sun and sea, or a city that feels loose and improvised; this one runs on precision.
munich.teaser: A city of gardens and galleries, with the Alps an hour past the last tram stop.

nairobi-mara.weather_note: July-October for the Great Migration and dry-season game viewing; January-February for calving and clear skies. Avoid the long rains of April-May.
nairobi-mara.perfect_if: You want the definitive African safari — the Migration, private conservancies and camps where the wild comes to your veranda.
nairobi-mara.skip_if: You need city polish and predictability; the Mara is about early mornings, dust and the untamed, not urban comforts.
nairobi-mara.teaser: The great herds on the move, watched from a tent where nothing stands between you and the plains.

copenhagen.weather_note: Go late May to early September for long, mild days and outdoor tables; winters are dark and cold, though December has a quiet festive charm.
copenhagen.perfect_if: You care about design, easy cycling streets and one of the best dining scenes in Europe, at a gentle unhurried pace.
copenhagen.skip_if: You want warmth, grandeur or a packed sightseeing list; Copenhagen rewards those who slow down, and it is not inexpensive.
copenhagen.teaser: A low, handsome city where design, the table and the water set the pace.

goa.weather_note: Golden and dry November to February; skip the June to September monsoon unless you want the green, empty version.
goa.perfect_if: You want a home-turf beach break that flexes from quiet North Goa villas to full-tilt nights with no visa or long-haul.
goa.skip_if: You want somewhere far from home or free of crowds in peak season; December Goa is busy and priced for it.
goa.teaser: The beaches everyone knows, done the way most people never bother to.

st-moritz.weather_note: December to March for snow and the frozen-lake season; July-August for hiking. Avoid the shoulder mud months of May and November when much closes.
st-moritz.perfect_if: You want the Alps at their most polished — long lunches on the piste, cashmere afternoons, and a grand old hotel where the staff remember your name.
st-moritz.skip_if: You are chasing a lively nightlife scene or an affordable ski week; this is a small, formal, expensive village that sleeps early.
st-moritz.teaser: The Engadine's high valley, where winter light and old-world hotels have drawn the same families for generations.

vienna.weather_note: Late spring and early autumn are mildest; December has the Christmas markets. Avoid the grey, cold depths of January-February unless you want the opera season indoors.
vienna.perfect_if: You want imperial grandeur, world-class music and museums, and coffee-house afternoons at an unhurried pace.
vienna.skip_if: You are after beaches, wild landscapes or nightlife-driven energy rather than culture and refinement.
vienna.teaser: The last great imperial capital, where the coffee house is an institution and the opera never really closed.

kochi.weather_note: Pleasant and dry October-March; avoid the June-September monsoon downpours.
kochi.perfect_if: You want Kerala's history and harbour life as a gentle gateway to the backwaters.
kochi.skip_if: You want nightlife or a beach holiday; this is a quiet, cultural port town.
kochi.teaser: A trading port layered with Portuguese, Dutch and Malabar histories, where the water still sets the pace.

rishikesh.weather_note: Best in spring and autumn; skip the peak summer heat and the July-August monsoon.
rishikesh.perfect_if: You want the Ganges, yoga and a serious wellness retreat within reach of Delhi.
rishikesh.skip_if: You drink and want nightlife; the town is largely vegetarian and alcohol-free.
rishikesh.teaser: The Ganges emerges from the hills here, and with it a quieter way of keeping time.

mauritius-city.weather_note: Cooler, drier and calm May-November; avoid the January-March cyclone season.
mauritius-city.perfect_if: You want a beach and resort holiday with familiar food and no visa friction.
mauritius-city.skip_if: You want dense culture or a city break; this is a resort island, best taken slowly.
mauritius-city.teaser: Lagoons, sugarcane and grand old resorts, with a plate of dal never far away.

las-vegas.weather_note: Comfortable in spring and autumn; the desert summer is brutally hot.
las-vegas.perfect_if: You want shows, dining and the Grand Canyon on a wider American trip.
las-vegas.skip_if: You dislike crowds and casinos; the appeal is loud and unapologetic.
las-vegas.teaser: A city built for the evening, with the desert's grandest canyon a short drive away.

darjeeling.weather_note: Clearest mountain views in spring and autumn; the monsoon brings mist and landslides.
darjeeling.perfect_if: You want tea gardens, the toy train and Kanchenjunga on a cool hill escape.
darjeeling.skip_if: You need a fast, direct journey; getting up the hill takes patience.
darjeeling.teaser: Tea estates unfold beneath the third-highest peak on earth, reached by a century-old railway.

munnar.weather_note: Cool and green September-March; the monsoon closes in from June to August.
munnar.perfect_if: You want rolling tea hills and cool air within a short drive of the Kerala coast.
munnar.skip_if: You want beaches or nightlife; this is a quiet, high-country tea town.
munnar.teaser: Tea carpets the hills for miles here, and the air turns cool the moment you climb.

jodhpur.weather_note: Best in the cool winter months; avoid the fierce desert summer from April to June.
jodhpur.perfect_if: You want the blue city, a mighty fort and a palace hotel that once housed a maharaja.
jodhpur.skip_if: You want greenery or a beach; this is desert Rajasthan, dry and monumental.
jodhpur.teaser: The blue city gathers below Mehrangarh, where a working palace still takes guests.

dublin.weather_note: Mildest and brightest May-September; the winter is grey, wet and short on daylight.
dublin.perfect_if: You want literary pubs, warm company and a base for Ireland's green coast.
dublin.skip_if: You want sunshine and grand monuments; Dublin's charm is human, not spectacular.
dublin.teaser: A city of writers and easy conversation, where the pub is the drawing room.

queenstown.weather_note: Warm and long-lit December-March; June-August brings ski season and cold.
queenstown.perfect_if: You want mountains and lakes with adventure or fine wine at the doorstep.
queenstown.skip_if: You want a short-haul trip; New Zealand is a long way for anything under a week.
queenstown.teaser: A lake ringed by mountains, equal parts adrenaline and quiet Central Otago wine.

osaka.weather_note: Cherry blossom in early April and crisp maples in November; the summer is hot and humid.
osaka.perfect_if: You want Japan's kitchen, a lively city and an easy hop to Kyoto and Nara.
osaka.skip_if: You are strictly vegetarian and inflexible; dashi and seafood run through the cuisine.
osaka.teaser: Japan's kitchen city, brash and appetite-forward, minutes from Kyoto's calm.

jaipur.weather_note: Best in the cool winter months; summer is scorching and the monsoon light is soft.
jaipur.perfect_if: You want the pink city's palaces, forts and the polish of the Golden Triangle.
jaipur.skip_if: You want nature or quiet; Jaipur is grand, busy and steeped in commerce.
jaipur.teaser: The pink city of palaces and forts, the jewel of the Golden Triangle.

nice-riviera.weather_note: Warm sea and calmer crowds in late spring and September; July-August is hot and busy.
nice-riviera.perfect_if: You want the Riviera: the sea, the light, and Monaco and Cannes at hand.
nice-riviera.skip_if: You want budget or solitude; this coast trades on glamour and it prices accordingly.
nice-riviera.teaser: The Cote d'Azur at its most composed, with Monaco and Cannes a short drive along the coast.

mahe-seychelles.weather_note: Calmest seas and clearest skies in April-May and October-November, between the trade winds.
mahe-seychelles.perfect_if: You want granite-boulder beaches and rare seclusion, visa-free, with Mumbai close.
mahe-seychelles.skip_if: You want nightlife or sightseeing; the islands reward stillness and swimming.
mahe-seychelles.teaser: Granite boulders, empty sands and rare quiet, visa-free from India.

salzburg.weather_note: Green and mild in summer, magical at Christmas; late winter is grey and quiet.
salzburg.perfect_if: You want Mozart, baroque streets and the Alps rising at the edge of a small city.
salzburg.skip_if: You want a big-city buzz; Salzburg is compact and best taken slowly.
salzburg.teaser: Mozart's baroque city between the river and the mountains, loveliest at Christmas.

sydney.weather_note: Warm and bright in the Australian spring and autumn; the summer holidays are hot and busy.
sydney.perfect_if: You want harbour, beaches and a polished city with excellent Indian food, direct from Delhi.
sydney.skip_if: You want a short-haul trip; Australia is far and deserves more than a few days.
sydney.teaser: A harbour city of beaches and good living, now a direct flight from Delhi.

mumbai.weather_note: Cool, dry November to February is the window; avoid the June-September monsoon and the humid pre-monsoon heat.
mumbai.perfect_if: You want India's most cosmopolitan city — colonial architecture, serious restaurants, a real night out and sea-facing suites at the Taj or Four Seasons.
mumbai.skip_if: You are after quiet, nature or a slow escape; Mumbai is dense, loud and relentless.
mumbai.teaser: The city that never quite sleeps, seen from a suite above the Arabian Sea.

istanbul.weather_note: Spring and early autumn are the most pleasant; July and August are hot and crowded, winter grey and wet.
istanbul.perfect_if: You want a great world city where two continents meet — Byzantine domes, the Bosphorus, and food that alone justifies the trip.
istanbul.skip_if: You want a beach or a quiet resort week; this is a city that asks to be walked and worked.
istanbul.teaser: Where Europe and Asia meet across the water — Hagia Sophia, the Bosphorus at dusk, and a table that never disappoints.

cappadocia.weather_note: Spring and autumn give the clearest ballooning weather; summer is hot and winter cold, though snow over the valleys is its own reward.
cappadocia.perfect_if: You want the balloons at dawn and a cave suite for two — a short, romantic add-on to Istanbul.
cappadocia.skip_if: You need more than a couple of days of things to do, or the balloons are the whole reason and weather cancels flights.
cappadocia.teaser: Dawn over the fairy chimneys with a hundred balloons rising — brief, singular, and best paired with Istanbul.

edinburgh.weather_note: Late spring through early autumn is kindest; August brings the festivals but also crowds. Winters are dark, wet and cold.
edinburgh.perfect_if: You want a walkable, literary old city with castle views, whisky, and easy reach into the Highlands.
edinburgh.skip_if: You are chasing sun, beaches or reliably warm weather.
edinburgh.teaser: A city of dark stone and long light, where the castle keeps watch and the Highlands begin just beyond.

buenos-aires.weather_note: Autumn in March to April and spring in October to November are best. Avoid the humid January heat.
buenos-aires.perfect_if: You want tango, exceptional steak and Malbec, and a European-feeling city at the far edge of the map.
buenos-aires.skip_if: You keep strictly vegetarian or want a short flight; this is a long haul into a meat-and-wine city.
buenos-aires.teaser: A city of late dinners, tango and Malbec, worth every hour of the journey to reach it.

bengaluru.weather_note: The cool, clear months from November to February are the best. Avoid the June to September monsoon showers.
bengaluru.perfect_if: You want a mild-weather city break with strong food, craft bars and easy weekend escapes into the hills.
bengaluru.skip_if: You are after monuments or beaches; this is a garden city built for living, not sightseeing.
bengaluru.teaser: The garden city, at its best over an easy dinner with the hills a short drive away.

cancun.weather_note: December to April is dry and warm; avoid the June to October hurricane and humidity season.
cancun.perfect_if: You hold a US or Schengen visa and want Caribbean water, Mayan ruins and a full week of resort ease.
cancun.skip_if: You have only a few days; it is a long haul and only pays off with a proper stretch on the ground.
cancun.teaser: Caribbean water and cenotes, with Chichen Itza and the quieter reaches of Tulum a short drive down the coast.

chennai.weather_note: November to February is the pleasant window; avoid the fierce April to June heat and the October monsoon.
chennai.perfect_if: You want deep South Indian temple culture, Chettinad cooking and Marina Beach at a gentle domestic pace.
chennai.skip_if: You are after a resort holiday or nightlife; this is a working city, best for its heritage and its food.
chennai.teaser: The gateway to the temple south, where Carnatic music, filter coffee and granite gopurams keep their own slow time.

marrakech.weather_note: Spring and autumn are ideal; avoid July-August peak heat and the cold desert nights of deep winter.
marrakech.perfect_if: You want a riad courtyard, a hammam, and the theatre of the medina within an easy flight of an Atlas Mountains escape.
marrakech.skip_if: You need a beach holiday or expect a polished, sanitised city; the souks are intense and the hustle is real.
marrakech.teaser: A walled city of courtyards and colour, where a private riad turns the medina's clamour into calm the moment the door closes.

zanzibar.weather_note: Go June to October for dry, calm days; avoid the long rains of March to May.
zanzibar.perfect_if: You want white-sand indulgence paired with a spice-island soul, ideally bookended with a mainland safari.
zanzibar.skip_if: You want a lively city break or reliably kosher-clean street food and nightlife on tap.
zanzibar.teaser: An Indian Ocean island where dhows still catch the wind and the days ask nothing of you.

agra.weather_note: October to March is clear and cool; summers are brutally hot.
agra.perfect_if: You want the Taj at dawn and a night in a view-facing suite.
agra.skip_if: You want more than a day or two — Agra is a single, perfect stop.
agra.teaser: One monument, seen properly, is worth the trip.

amritsar.weather_note: Cool, clear winters are best; avoid the searing summer.
amritsar.perfect_if: You want the Golden Temple at first light and the finest Punjabi food there is.
amritsar.skip_if: You want beaches, nightlife or a long stay.
amritsar.teaser: Gold on water, and a langar that feeds thousands.

andaman.weather_note: November to April is dry and calm; the monsoon runs May to September.
andaman.perfect_if: You want white sand and clear water without leaving the country or arranging a visa.
andaman.skip_if: You want cities, culture or nightlife.
andaman.teaser: India's own castaway coast, an ocean away from the mainland.

jaisalmer.weather_note: October to February is the only comfortable window; the desert summer is extreme.
jaisalmer.perfect_if: You want a golden fort city and a night under the dunes in a luxury desert camp.
jaisalmer.skip_if: You want greenery, water or a fast pace.
jaisalmer.teaser: A sandcastle city that turns to gold at sundown.

kolkata.weather_note: Cool, dry winters are ideal; summers and the monsoon are humid.
kolkata.perfect_if: You want the most literary, coffee-house city in India and its extraordinary food.
kolkata.skip_if: You want polish, beaches or nightlife.
kolkata.teaser: India's city of ideas, warm and worn and wide awake.

leh-ladakh.weather_note: June to September is the only real window; passes and roads close in winter. Acclimatise for altitude.
leh-ladakh.perfect_if: You want high-desert monasteries, thin blue air and the drama of the Himalaya.
leh-ladakh.skip_if: You have heart or altitude concerns, or want comfort over rawness.
leh-ladakh.teaser: A moonscape at 11,000 feet, monasteries clinging to the rock.

los-angeles.weather_note: Warm and dry most of the year; spring and autumn are the sweet spots.
los-angeles.perfect_if: You want beaches, studios and canyon-view hotels, and don't mind the drive everywhere.
los-angeles.skip_if: You want a walkable city or a short flight.
los-angeles.teaser: Sun, screens and hillside pools — if you're willing to drive for them.

manali.weather_note: Spring and early summer are green and mild; winter brings snow but harder access.
manali.perfect_if: You want mountains, orchards and river valleys a short hop from Delhi.
manali.skip_if: You want to avoid crowds in peak season, or want a beach.
manali.teaser: Apple valleys and snow lines, an hour's flight from the plains.

melbourne.weather_note: Autumn and spring are kindest; the city is famous for four seasons in a day.
melbourne.perfect_if: You want laneway coffee, world-class dining and wine country an hour away.
melbourne.skip_if: You want reliable sun or a short flight.
melbourne.teaser: Australia's most liveable city, and its best table.

miami.weather_note: November to April is warm and dry; summer is hot, humid and hurricane-prone.
miami.perfect_if: You want art-deco beaches, Latin energy and a serious nightlife.
miami.skip_if: You want culture, quiet or a manageable flight.
miami.teaser: Ocean Drive, Design District and the party that never quite ends.

paro.weather_note: Spring and autumn are clear and mild; a daily sustainable-tourism fee applies.
paro.perfect_if: You want the Tiger's Nest, empty valleys and Aman-grade calm.
paro.skip_if: You want nightlife, shopping or a beach.
paro.teaser: A Buddhist kingdom that measures itself in happiness, not haste.

ranthambore.weather_note: October to April for game drives; the park closes in the monsoon.
ranthambore.perfect_if: You want a genuine chance of a wild tiger and a tented camp to match Africa's best.
ranthambore.skip_if: You need certainty — sightings are never guaranteed.
ranthambore.teaser: India's best odds on a wild tiger, from a camp worth the airfare.

rio-de-janeiro.weather_note: December to March is warm and lively; Carnival is February or early March.
rio-de-janeiro.perfect_if: You want Copacabana, Sugarloaf and Carnival, and will travel far for them.
rio-de-janeiro.skip_if: You want a short, easy or low-key trip.
rio-de-janeiro.teaser: Mountains, sea and samba — the most dramatic setting of any city.

shimla.weather_note: Spring and early summer are pleasant; winter can bring snow and harder access.
shimla.perfect_if: You want a colonial hill station, the toy train and cool pine air near Delhi.
shimla.skip_if: You want to dodge peak-season crowds, or want a beach.
shimla.teaser: The Raj's summer capital, still cool under the deodars.

srinagar.weather_note: Late spring for tulips and gardens, autumn for chinar colour; winter is cold and snowbound.
srinagar.perfect_if: You want a shikara on Dal Lake, a heritage houseboat and Mughal gardens in bloom.
srinagar.skip_if: You want nightlife or guaranteed year-round access.
srinagar.teaser: Lake, gardens and mountains — the valley the Mughals called paradise.
